Copying from the ACDE call: Could we know how 8130 composes with zkzkframes, recent roots, keyed nonces and transaction assertions? By proxy this should allow us to know how incorporating any of the 8130 ideas into 8141 will affect the above.

Sidenote: If we do compare 8130 and 8141, I think it would be also be constructive to discuss the difference in requirements as a starting point before diving into the specifics of each proposal
Sounds good @kevaundray will have it all ready!

~I'l like to discuss moving from using a special-target-VERIFY frame for the expiry mechanism, to using a new frame mode. Spec'd here: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12198~

Happy to have the topic postponed if we're not yet ready to discuss such specific frame-related topics.

I might not be able to make the call, but would like to call attention to my 8130 amendment here: 
https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8130-account-abstraction-by-account-configurations/25952/27

On behalf of Offchain: 

We are very happy that ACD is considering Native AA as a headliner, and think it is essential for L1 to adopt it in Hegota. 

We wanted to outline practical next steps of things we would need to see in 8141 for Offchain to be able to implement it for Arbitrum Nitro*. As a quick reminder, we weigh Native AA designs against four considerations: possible throughput, DoS vectors at transaction admission, DevEx, and UX/security from a wallet interface perspective. The core requirement behind our asks is a payment must be guaranteed at admission time through a bounded, statically verifiable path.

1) [Required] Pure verification frames as the default admission path: Verification can stay programmable, but no external state reads, bounded cost, bounded result. We support the signature-verification-only direction for validation frames and want it normative in the spec. We are directly working with EF, EthLabs, Base, and WalletConnect on this direction.
2) [Nice-to-have] a Guarantor mechanism, as an optional but ‘officially’ supported extension, including a payer-only verify variant where the payer covers verification gas even if a later sender VERIFY fails. We will create an EIP for this.

Offchain is reviewing the prospect of proposing that the Arbitrum DAO adopt 8130 first: 8130 provides these admission-time guarantees today, covers the dominant user flows, and it does not prevent adding 8141 later. We will reconsider implementing 8141 alongside 8130 once the spec stabilizes with the changes above and ships on L1. We think 8130 deserves genuine consideration in this headliner process, but we are not explicitly asking ACD to adopt it; if ACD converges on a modified 8141 for L1, we will support this effort and may adopt it also. A single standard shared across L1 and L2s would be ideal, but we do not see it as required. What matters most to us is that Native AA standards are implemented with L2s in mind, and in compatible ways, so wallets and infra can support them.

*Disclaimer: Statements regarding product roadmap, planned functionality, developments in progress, potential proposals, and future direction are forward-looking, reflect current expectations only, and are not commitments or guarantees. Any upgrades to Arbitrum One or Nova require standard AIP governance process. Other dedicated blockchains built with Arbitrum Platform can adopt features at their own discretion once integrated with Arbitrum Nitro.
